held.gap_is_real: The bank has no Oil Record Book card. 46 cards mention the ORB and none teaches it. This is a genuine, high-value gap.
held.why_held: The code list cannot be published as current. The held base MEPC.117(52) gives Part I sections A-I and Part II sections A-R, but a widely repeated secondary claim attributes a 2016/2018 revision of the ORB entry codes to MEPC.276(70) - and obtaining that resolution showed it amends appendix II Form B only. MEPC.277(70) is Annex V and MEPC.316(74) is Annex VI. The actual ORB amendment is not identified and not held, so the A-to-I list may be superseded. Publishing it would repeat the BMP5 defect exactly: an authoritative base that is stale for the one provision being taught.
held.registered_as: RQ-A1 in the shared corpus review queue, against 03-imo-instruments/MARPOL-Annex-I
held.unblocks_when: The amending resolution is located from IMO's MEPC index or the depositary list and the Part I / Part II code lists are re-verified against it.
held.unblocked_by: The independent reviewer identified MEPC.187(59) - adopted 17 July 2009, deemed accepted 1 July 2010, in force 1 January 2011 - 'Amendments to regulations 1, 12, 13, 17 and 38 of MARPOL Annex I, Supplement to the IOPP Certificate and Oil Record Book Parts I and II'. Verified from the resolution itself, acquired, and filed in the shared corpus. RQ-A1 CLOSED. It was one request away on the same IMO CDN pattern the corpus already documents - the hold was right on the merits and the search behind it was not thorough enough.
held.why_not_authored_now: The blocker is gone but the card is deliberately NOT written in this batch. It would ship without the independent review every other H3A card received, and an Oil Record Book card is exactly the kind a candidate recites verbatim in an oral. It is queued for the next batch, where it must be built from MEPC.187(59) and checked against MEPC.314(74) (electronic record books, in force 1 October 2020, RQ-A2, not held).
held.closure_note: CLOSED 2026-08-31 in run H3A-ORB. The hold protected a real defect: MEPC.187(59) replaced Part I sections (A)-(H) and Part II section (J) with effect from 1 January 2011 WITHOUT changing the section letters, so the 2004 list the corpus held would have read as current and would never have been challenged in an oral. (C) gained 'transfer'; (D) and (E) became 'starting of' discharge, transfer or disposal; reg. 17.2.3 gained the defined term 'oil residue (sludge)' and lost 'and other oil residues'. RQ-A2 was closed in the same pass by acquiring MEPC.314(74), which is what lets the card state that an electronic ORB must be APPROVED by the Administration rather than hedge.

H3A.local_corpus_demonstration: The Form A / Form B card needed NO web research for its substance. The allocation rule is quoted from the Notes to both forms in Appendix II of the Revised MARPOL Annex I (MEPC.117(52)), already held in the shared desktop corpus with a full text layer - and it is SHARPER than the shorthand every summary repeats: Form B covers oil tankers AND non-tankers with regulation 2.2 cargo tanks, keyed to the three ship types the IOPP Certificate itself categorises. Only the currentness check went outside, and it returned MEPC.276(70), which is now preserved in that corpus and added to its amendment chain.

FAST.identity: RESOLVED FROM THE MAKER. Wartsila service catalogue, 2-stroke engine services, FAST upgrade page: "Fuel Activated Sacless Technology (FAST)". NOTE THE SPELLING - Wartsila writes SACLESS with one c, and secondary write-ups give "Sackless" and "Fuel Actuated", both wrong against the maker. A candidate who expands the acronym the way the trade press does will be expanding it wrongly.
facts_from_maker: prolonged injector needle and adapted nozzle atomizer
reduces the sac volume by up to 90%
all fuel per cycle injected at full injection pressure for improved atomization
hydrocarbon and carbon monoxide emissions significantly reduced
part-load fuel consumption lowered by up to 1%
time between overhauls lengthened up to 18,000 running hours
applies to Wartsila RT-flex 2-stroke families, not to MAN engines
FAST.authority: Wartsila service catalogue, 2-stroke engine services, FAST upgrade page - the maker is the primary authority for its own product. This is MAKER guidance, not regulation, and must be presented as such.
FAST.converges_with: AUG-0160. FAST is itself a CII-improvement technology - Wartsila anticipates a 5% CII improvement from FAST combined with Part Load Optimisation and Intelligent Combustion Control - so one CII-technologies card can carry FAST as a named example and answer both asks without a second root.

APEX.identity: RESOLVED FROM THE PRIMARY SOURCE. DGS MS Notice 9 of 2014, section 6.2 "SMS Manuals", retrieved from dgma.gov.in and read. 6.2.1.1 verbatim: "The Apex Manual of the company is to be referred to as “Safety Management Manual” and is required to be in compliance with the various elements of the ISM Code, as amended. The manual must contain Policies, objectives, organization structure, responsibilities & authorities of relevant personnel, communication level and identification, risk assessment and control of processes of the company and on board the ship with respect to ISM Code. The manual shall be so prepared that frequent amendment to the manual is avoided." 6.2.1.2: where other operational manuals, instructions, checklists and forms form part of the SMS, "the apex manual shall contain cross references to all those documents". 6.2.1.3: the SMS manuals shall address applicable codes and non-mandatory instruments per MSC.1/Circ.1371, and the basic elements of the Shipboard Occupational Health and Safety Programme and fatigue guidance (MSC/Circ.1014). 6.2.1.4: the apex manual "can have provision to indicate reference to other relevant manuals / documents".
APEX.caution_already_recorded_in_the_notes: The same notes warn that the Notice does NOT split the manual into named Tier 1/2/3 categories, while the notes index elsewhere says "ISM Apex Manual - 3 Tiers". The tiering is a common industry presentation, not the Notice's language, and a card must not present it as the Notice's.
APEX.outstanding: CLOSED. The notice has been opened and read. Three points settled against it. (1) TIERING: the word apex appears five times in 33 pages and there is NO Tier 1/2/3 language anywhere - the MIW oralnotes caution is confirmed, and a card must present tiering as industry practice, never as the Notice’s. (2) DATE: the notice’s own first page reads "Dated: 15.05.2014". The MIW oralnotes are RIGHT and the DGMA website listing, which shows it as issued 06-Mar-2014, is wrong. Cite 15 May 2014. (3) A CITATION ERROR IN OUR OWN NOTES, found by opening the source: the oralnotes give this notice the file number "No. ENG/ISM/59(4)/97". The PDF shows that number as the reference for MS NOTICE 28 OF 2003, listed in section 4.3 among the notices this one supersedes - not as this notice’s own number. Do not carry ENG/ISM/59(4)/97 into a card as the 2014 notice’s reference. Section 4.3 also confirms the supersession claim: MS Notice 09 of 2003, MS Notice 28 of 2003 and a schedule of DGS Engineering Circulars.
APEX.currentness: CHECKED AT THE ISSUER. DGMA published a DRAFT Addendum to MS Notice 09 of 2014 dated 05 September 2025 (File No. 13-44012/2/2025-ENGG), subject "Strengthened Regulatory Framework for Interim Document of Compliance". It was retrieved and read: it contains ZERO occurrences of apex and does not touch section 6.2. So the apex-manual definition stands unamended - and, being a DRAFT, the addendum must not be cited as being in force.
APEX.access_note: indiacode.nic.in refused the connection (ECONNREFUSED). No attempt was made to work around it; the document was obtained instead from DGMA’s own current domain dgma.gov.in, which is the authoritative publisher.
